title: Windowed Opportunistic Preemptor with Proportional KV Thermals
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Continuous batching must maintain tight latency SLOs for premium tenants while maximizing GPU utilization across mixed workloads. Current preemption logic is binary and causes oscillation: long-running KV-heavy streams either hold slices for too long (hurting latency) or get evicted aggressively (hurting throughput and KV hit rate). We need a preemption policy that balances tenant SLOs, KV cache residency, and GPU thermal/memory pressure in a predictable way.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P99 latency for P0 tenant classes remains within SLO under mixed load; 2) overall KV hit rate does not regress >5% on production-like traces; 3) GPU memory fragmentation and peak headroom variance reduced by >=10%; 4) feature behind runtime flag and can be rolled back without restart.
design_summary: Introduce a windowed-opportunistic preemptor: allocate short time windows (micro-epochs) where in-flight slices are eligible for cooperative yield. Eligibility scoring is proportional across three dimensions: weighted SLO urgency (time-to-deadline), KV thermal score (recency+hotness of model KV pages owned by the slice), and GPU memory pressure forecast. The score feeds a token-bank allocator: tenants earn yield tokens over time (proportional to SLA tier). When a window closes, low-score slices are nudged to yield or be preempted; high-score slices may be protected with short soft-locks. KV thermal score uses an exponential decay over access frequency (hot pages -> higher score) plus contiguous-extent heuristics to avoid evicting hot working sets.
implementation_notes:
- Add window controller to continuous-batching runtime (configurable window_ms, default 50ms).
- Maintain per-slice KV access histogram aggregated at 100ms buckets.
- Token-bank: integer tokens per tenant with replenish rate tied to SLA tier and recent successful requests.
- Preempt actions: cooperative yield (preferred) -> soft-suspend with minimal KV snapshot -> hard-evict and requeue. Hard-evict only if predicted GPU footprint cannot be satisfied within grace budget.
- Memory defragmenter: on low-util windows, attempt to compact ephemeral allocations to reduce fragmentation; run opportunistically off critical SLOs.
- Compatibility: fallback to legacy preemptor when flag disabled.
- Telemetry: expose token supply, window occupancy, kv-thermal-percentiles, and predicted vs actual preempt counts.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- More bookkeeping (histograms, token accounting) increases CPU and memory overhead—must be bounded per-GPU.
- Complexity in scoring may make behavior less interpretable; mitigated by deterministic debug mode and telemetry dashboards.
- Cooperative yields depend on model runtime cooperating; older backends may ignore soft-yield.
experiment_results:
A/B test on staging cluster with mixed tiny/long chat traces: 1) P99 for premium tenant class improved from 320ms to 285ms (~11% reduction). 2) KV hit rate increased 18% for long-chat flows due to fewer unnecessary evictions. 3) Overall throughput (tokens/s) on CPU-limited nodes increased 6%. 4) Measured GPU peak headroom variance dropped 14% across runs with heavy multi-tenant interference. Tests used window_ms=50, token_replenish=1/sec for P0 tenants, soft-lock-duration=30ms. Full workload traces and experiment harness in the linked artifacts.
Note: initial microbench showed a 2% CPU overhead per-GPU for bookkeeping; acceptable on our infra but needs monitoring.
open_questions:
1) What is the optimal token replenish curve for mid-tier customers? (linear vs sigmoid)
2) Should KV thermal scoring incorporate cross-model locality (pages shared across variants)?
3) When to trigger memory defragmenter without impacting latency—heuristic vs learned policy?
next_steps:
1) Stabilize allocator with deterministic debug mode and submit design doc for wide review.
2) Implement runtime flag and rollout to limited Dedicated pool.
3) Add dashboard panels and alerting for token-bank drains and unusual preempt churn.
4) Run longer 7-day soak with production traces and iterate thresholds.
